questions.text: What is unique about the current rate of climate change?
opts: It's the fastest in 65 million years
questions.correct: It's the fastest in 65 million years
questions.hint: "Changes occurring at a rate not seen in the geological record for at least 65 million years."

questions.text: What happened to the Aral Sea?
opts: It was drained by Soviet irrigation projects
questions.correct: It was drained by Soviet irrigation projects
questions.hint: "The Aral Sea was drained by Soviet-era irrigation projects over the second half of the twentieth century."

questions.text: Why is the saiga antelope described as a conservation success?
opts: It was saved by a single law
Its population went from near-extinction to over a million
questions.correct: Its population went from near-extinction to over a million
questions.hint: "By 2023, the population had grown back to over a million. One of the great conservation success stories."

questions.text: Conservation programmes that exclude local communities work best.
questions.hint: "Conservation programmes that do not include local communities have consistently failed."

questions.text: The Tian Shan glaciers are a critical source of ___ for the region.
questions.hint: "These glaciers are a critical source of FRESH WATER for the region."

questions.text: According to the text, what is understanding climate science?
opts: The literacy of the 21st century for all fields
questions.correct: The literacy of the 21st century for all fields
questions.hint: "Understanding the science is not optional. It is the literacy of the twenty-first century."

questions.text: What first made Aizhan aware of environmental issues?
opts: The Ural River getting lower and fish disappearing near her village
questions.correct: The Ural River getting lower and fish disappearing near her village
questions.hint: "Every summer I could see the river was lower... The fish were disappearing."

questions.text: What was found to have been released into the river?
questions.hint: "A factory was found to have been releasing untreated chemicals into the river."

questions.text: What is Aizhan's current main focus?
questions.hint: "Water rights. Communities in rural Kazakhstan are being denied clean water."

questions.text: What gives Aizhan hope?
opts: Young people caring more about the environment
questions.correct: Young people caring more about the environment
questions.hint: "More young Kazakhstanis care about the environment than ever before... That gives me hope."

questions.text: Aizhan says the attitude of young people has been ___ by climate news.
questions.hint: "The attitude has been CHANGED by climate news, by what they can see with their own eyes."

questions.text: Aizhan says the river cleanup was completed quickly after the factory closed.
questions.hint: "The cleanup hasn't been completed — the riverbed is still being studied. It will take years."

questions.text: "Water IS TESTED daily." — This is:
questions.hint: "is tested" = is + pp = Present Simple Passive. ✅ Routine/regular action.

questions.text: "The river IS BEING CLEANED." — This is:
questions.hint: "is being cleaned" = is + being + pp = Present Continuous Passive. ✅ Action ongoing now.

questions.text: "Several parks ___ (establish) in Kazakhstan recently." (Present Perfect Passive)
questions.hint: Recent completion → Present Perfect Passive: "HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED." ✅

questions.text: "Emissions MUST BE reduced." — "must be reduced" is:
questions.hint: modal (must) + be + past participle = Modal Passive. ✅

questions.text: "She has an impact ___ the environment."
questions.hint: "impact ON the environment." ✅ Always "on" with impact.

questions.text: "Deforestation contributes ___ climate change."
questions.hint: "contribute TO climate change." ✅ Always "to."

questions.text: "We must ___ climate change urgently." (key verb)
questions.hint: "TACKLE climate change." ✅ Not "reduce climate change" — climate change is tackled/addressed.

questions.text: "At risk ___ extinction." Correct preposition:
questions.hint: "at risk OF extinction." ✅ Always "of" after "at risk."

questions.text: "The glaciers have retreated." "Retreated" means:
questions.hint: "retreat" = to move back; glaciers retreat as they lose ice and shrink.

questions.text: "Deployed at unprecedented scale." "Unprecedented" means:
opts: Never done before at this level
questions.correct: Never done before at this level
questions.hint: "unprecedented" = never seen or done before to this extent.

questions.text: "Commercial poaching was widespread." "Poaching" means:
questions.hint: "poaching" = illegally killing or capturing animals, often commercially.

questions.text: "Conservation efforts produced a remarkable recovery." "Conservation" means:
questions.hint: "conservation" = protection, preservation, and sustainable management of the natural world.

questions.text: "The scientific consensus is clear." "Consensus" means:
opts: General agreement among the scientific community
questions.correct: General agreement among the scientific community
questions.hint: "consensus" = broad agreement; what most experts agree on.
